note: Many disputed rows were questions during the drill (is it X or Y?) - dropped per the reader brief. D4/D5 are the masc/fem adjective after مرة: one voiced (D4), one let pass (D5). D14 folded into D15. A2's t_amal (06:10) comes before his line (06:43); the transcript order is odd there, timing only.

row.why: 'Let's see if I did them right' needs iza; she stopped him and asked 'إنه or إذا?', pointing at the linker.
row.english: Now let's see if I did them right.

rulings.why: Her 'إنه، or إذا؟' right after his line is a voiced prompt on the linker; 'see if' takes iza.
Not a clear error: Amal asked about working from home today (08:33 كيف الشغل بالبيت) and 'لا، بشتغل بس، نمت أكثر' reads fine as 'no, I am working, I just slept more'.

row.why: Describing today's clothes he used the bare form with no b- (بلبس, or the participle لابس); she let it pass. Engine may have dropped the b-.

rulings.why: Bare البس in a statement about today; low because the engine can drop b-.

row.why: مرة is feminine so the adjective after it is el-oola; he said el awwal at 18:43, 19:04 and 20:54, Amal recast المرة الأولى إلي at 20:58 and he said 'El mara el ula ... you didn't correct me on the other one'.

rulings.why: Real and separate from A4 (andi -> إلي): a different wrong piece. One row at the first try (18:43); her recast at 20:58 fixed it and he took it.

row.medi_said: and then el thani, el aw- el mara el thani, yeah, is also second time.
row.why: After feminine مرة the adjective is el-tanye (and marra tanye at 23:04); Amal discussed the meaning and let the form pass - the same slip she then caught with الأولى.

rulings.why: Masculine adjective after feminine مرة, twice (22:22, 23:04); she never voiced a fix, so grammar-B, one row.

row.why: He knew it was 'our' (34:22 'the end of our schedule') but put -ha on برنامج; Amal recast برنامجنا and he repeated it.

rulings.why: A separate pronoun-ending slip from A11 (the aa5er structure); her 'بس برنامجنا' is a voiced recast.
A question about the rule ('It's a olin? ... Is this plural?'), not a production; the agreed rows A12/A13 already hold the slips of this drill.

row.amal_said: Very close. What's questions? ... Mm-hmm. أسألتك.
row.why: He had the word أسئلة (Amal: 'very close') but dropped the -t before the owner ending; she prompted 'What's questions?' and he said أسيليتك, she confirmed أسألتك.

rulings.why: Grammar A3, not vocab: 'very close' shows he had the plural; the missing piece is the feminine -t before -ak, which he added after her prompt.

row.why: He put the -ik ending on عن and then a noun; after her 'then everyone' he said 'ghayr ann ikul' and she said Yes.

rulings.why: Her English prompt is a voiced signal (PG-22); he fixed it to عن الكل and she confirmed.
Not a correction: 'Or that's like, um, unique maybe. Yeah.' explains what طالب مختلف means and accepts it; طالب مختلف is a valid phrase.

row.medi_said: راح. This will be راح يكون الـأخر-- ... أخر مرة
row.amal_said: Only one correction is مرة، مرة is feminine or masculine. So راح شو؟
row.why: ykoon must match feminine مرة; Amal named the gender of مرة and he said راح تكون.
row.english: It will be the last time.

rulings.why: Both readers agree on the slip; B9 (person on ykoon) is the exact rule - ykoon matching its subject.

row.amal_said: You don't need منكون، خلص، بس سيئين.
row.why: 'Bad at choosing' needs bi + the noun (بالاختيار); he put the bare verb بنختار after the adjective and she let that part pass (she fixed نكون and سيء, A18/A19).
row.english: We are both bad at choosing.

rulings.why: Different piece from A18/A19; she did not touch بنختار, so grammar-B, low.

row.why: 'I kept using a lot of Arabic words' needs the plural كلمات; she laughed and let it pass. Low: garbled line.
row.english: (I kept using) a lot of Arabic words.

rulings.why: Singular كلمة with كتير for many words; low because the line is garbled.
Folded into D15: he dropped قريب himself (switched to قبل at 1:05:43) before any fix; her later آخر / الشهر الماضي answers the one intended phrase 'last month', held in D15.

row.medi_said: قبل شهر، uh, ما، ما استعملت اسباني كتير.
row.amal_said: Do, do you wanna say the last month؟ ... الشهر الماضي. ... قبل is for ago.
row.why: قبل + number = ago; for 'last month' it is الشهر الماضي. Amal asked if he meant 'the last month', led him to الماضي and explained قبل is for ago.
row.english: Last month I didn't use Spanish much.

rulings.why: Grammar E6, not vocab: he knows قبل; the slip is the ago-rule used where 'last' was meant, and Amal named it ('قبل is for ago').

row.medi_said: um, would I say صح or مزبوط؟ ... مزبوط. Yeah, right?
row.why: He asked which word for 'right' and leaned to مزبوط; Amal said صح is better.

rulings.why: A which-word question she answered by picking صح: a didn't-know, tier 0.
Cannot be verified: after 'Relax?' Amal said 'No. سبا-- bad word' and never supplied ارتاح in reply; ترتاح at 11:22 is six minutes later in another context.

row.medi_said: I agree. I don't know how to say I agree.
row.amal_said: We have, we have a saying-- مظبوط عادي، مظبوط.
row.why: He said he did not know 'I agree'; her reply starts with مظبوط. Low: her line runs into the saying she then quotes.

rulings.why: He asked how to say it and she gave مظبوط; tier 0, low.

row.amal_said: That's عمر. عمر، شو عمرك؟ قديش عمرك؟
row.why: He heard her العمر (age/life) as أمر (command); she asked 'What's عمر?' and taught it.

rulings.why: Listening miss of her word, she taught it; mode listening.
Not a slip: Amal set him up to try conjugating مرة ('try to conjugate it and tell me'), and 'Marti. Does this mean my woman?' is a question; she says it is 'technically right'.

row.medi_said: شنتة الـ آخر. Or آخر الشن-- no.
row.why: Asked for the second way to say 'her last bag' (after he got شنتة الأخيرة) he tried شنتة الـ آخر; Amal said 'No end, but something else' and gave آخر شنطة إلها.

rulings.why: A new wrong attempt 1.5 min after A8/A9, after he had got الأخيرة right; her 'No end' is an explicit no.
Not an error: لها is accepted elsewhere in this lesson (39:48 ثانية كاسا لها -> 'Great'); her آخر شنطة إلها at 33:43 finishes the phrase, it does not fix لها.
A question about the rule ('can you do ثانية كسرتها؟'); the real attempt is agreed row A14 at 39:29.
Pronunciation (S4): Ajwabetek already has the -t; ajwabetek vs ajwabtek is only a vowel, and he settled on ajwabtek.
Self-fix inside a question ('there's an N, right? طريقتني؟ No, طريقتي... I said it right') before Amal's لا.
Pronunciation (S4): بنطفأ / نطفا is his saying of ندفع (d/t, dropped ع) - he knows the word ('Oh yeah that's right'); the grammar of this line is agreed row A22.
Not a vocab fix: he asked which word to use in the sentence exercise and she answered 'whatever you want' (اللي بدك إياه).
A question about the rule ('آخر الوقت. Would this be the last time? Or can I use آخر الـ'); she answered the question.
Not an error: بوت on her sheet ('sneakers / boots | Boat | بوت') is the same word boot.
Cannot be verified: the engine often drops و; the year is said in passing, Amal did not react, and the line is garbled (عار استعاش).
